title: FHFA House Price Index — Monthly Index (July 2026 data)
source: FHFA: TWO primaries read direct 2026-09-06. (1) fhfa.gov/data/hpi (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes), the agency's own "2026 HPI Release Dates" block, row "Tuesday, September 29 | Monthly Index | July 2026". (2) The published 2026Q2 report PDF (fhfa.gov/document/d/hpi/fhfa-house-price-index-report-2026q2, HTTP 200, 1,522,949 bytes), whose Notes section reads verbatim "FHFA will release the next monthly HPI report (including data through July 2026) on September 29, 2026, and the next quarterly report ... on November 24, 2026" -- extracted from the PDF by this lane itself (pure-Python FlateDecode, since pdftotext is unavailable on this runner), NOT cited second-hand; the same PDF also embeds the full release-dates table carrying the identical Sept 29 row. Promoted estimate -> confirmed on the precedent the fhfa-hpi-2026-11-24 and fhfa-hpi-2026-10-27 lanes set: the no-self-confirm convention binds the sweep that DISCOVERED an event (fhfa-hpi-2026-10-27), not its independent second look. UNLIKE fhfa-hpi-2026-10-27, which is confirmed on ONE primary and says so, this date is named in prose by a published FHFA document AND in two forward tables. Structural corroboration: 2026-09-29 is the last Tuesday of September 2026, and the report archive is 68 of 68 last-Tuesday releases since 2021 (271-row archive, all 12 paginated pages, 1996-03-21 -> 2026-08-25, re-fetched and re-parsed by this lane). No release time is stated on either primary and none is claimed here. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: THE FAMILY'S BASE-SETTER: the July-2026 monthly is the nearest FHFA edition and the print that sets the comparison base both open sibling ledgers (fhfa-hpi-2026-10-27, fhfa-hpi-2026-11-24) explicitly defer to. This lane's own contribution is the REVISION STUDY neither sibling could run (both recorded pdftotext as unavailable; this lane read FHFA's own revision sentence out of 30 monthly report pages instead). Across 28 monthly reports 2023-01-31 -> 2026-07-28 that state one: 10 (36%) say the prior month "remained unchanged" and 18 (64%) report a revision -- 17 of those 18 are exactly 0.1 percentage point and one (2026-03-31, 0.1% -> 0.3%) is 0.2, with direction skewed 14 upward to 4 downward. So the base this print sets is soft by one tick roughly two-thirds of the time, and the softness leans up. TWO CROSS-LEDGER CORRECTIONS, both measurable: (1) the monthly/quarterly split since 2021 is 45/23, NOT the 48/20 the fhfa-hpi-2026-10-27 ledger reports -- FHFA's own release-type labels put every quarterly edition in Feb/May/Aug/Nov, which is 23 slots in this window; the seventeen FOMC-day-1 collision DATES are reproduced exactly, only the denominators move (17 of 45 = 37.8%, and 0 of 23 quarterly). (2) On the correctly-classified monthly-non-FOMC subset (n=28) DHI's session range is p=0.4089, not the p=0.0269 that ledger reports for a 31-day subset built from the 48/20 split. Impact LOW, symbols empty, and the tape null is the family's cleanest because it lands on the subset this print actually belongs to: 54 permutation tests (six subsets x nine instruments, 20,000 iterations, session high-low range since 2021) return two hits at p<0.05 against ~2.7 expected by chance -- LEN all-68 (p=0.0385, NARROWER, wrong sign) and PHM FOMC-day-1 (p=0.0431, a subset this print is NOT in) -- while the monthly-non-FOMC subset returns NOTHING across all nine instruments, minimum p=0.3058. This is not an FOMC day (the September FOMC is 15-16), but 'not FOMC' is not 'clean': 32 tracked events sit within five days -- more than the 22 around 10-27 -- the morning also carries JOLTS at 10:00 alongside the standing Conference Board Consumer Confidence confound (the only one of the three 2026 FHFA editions to do so), and the corridor carries four high-impact events plus a summit.
